title: The Best Score With Jumps of Up to k

concept.title: The best previous value in a sliding window
body: You stand at index 0 and want to reach index `n - 1`. From index `i` you can jump to any index from `i + 1` to `i + k`. Every index you land on adds its value to your score (the first one counts too), and you want the **largest total**. Let `dp[i]` be the best score for reaching `i`. Then `dp[i] = a[i] + max(dp[j])` over the previous `k` positions `j = i - k, ..., i - 1`.

Computing the maximum of the last `k` values for every `i` costs `k`. But this is exactly the **sliding window maximum**: keep a deque of indexes with **decreasing `dp` values**, remove the front when it is more than `k` positions away, and the front gives the maximum for `dp[i]`.

body.code:
dp[0] = a[0]; dq = [0]
for i in range(1, n):
    while dq[0] < i - k: dq.popleft()           # too far to jump from
    dp[i] = a[i] + dp[dq[0]]
    while dq and dp[dq[-1]] <= dp[i]: dq.pop()   # keep dp decreasing
    dq.append(i)

body: The scores can be negative, so you may have to take some bad cells; you always take the best path. Dynamic programming plus a monotonic queue turns an O(n * k) solution into O(n).

statement: You are at index 0 of an array of `n` integers (positive or negative) and want to reach index `n - 1`. In one jump you move forward by 1 to `k` places. Your score is the sum of the values of all indexes you stand on, including the first and the last one. Print the largest possible score.
hints: Let `dp[i]` be the best score that ends at index i.
`dp[i]` is `a[i]` plus the best `dp` of the previous `k` indexes.
Get that maximum with a deque of indexes with decreasing `dp` values.

explanation: `dp[i] = a[i] + max(dp[i-k..i-1])`. The maximum of the sliding window of `dp` values comes from a monotonic deque, so every step takes constant time.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, k = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

from collections import deque
dp = [0] * n
dp[0] = a[0]
dq = deque([0])
for i in range(1, n):
    while dq[0] < i - k:
        dq.popleft()
    dp[i] = a[i] + dp[dq[0]]
    while dq and dp[dq[-1]] <= dp[i]:
        dq.pop()
    dq.append(i)
print(dp[n - 1])
